title: Polyprecision Negotiator and Validation Pipeline for Mixed-Precision Kernel Dispatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a runtime component that negotiates between precision execution paths (FP16, FP8, INT8) at request time and validates the chosen path against accuracy constraints. This ticket implements the 'Polyprecision Negotiator' — a decision layer that consumes quantization profiles, lightweight online predictors, and calibration artifacts to select the most cost/latency-efficient kernel set while keeping model quality within guardrails. It also wires a validation pipeline that records per-profile accuracy deltas on a representative eval suite and triggers automated rollback or fallback when degradation exceeds thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator chooses an execution path (FP16/FP8/INT8) per-request based on latency budget and quality budget; decision logged for telemetry.
End-to-end eval on canonical benchmark (1000 prompt pairs) shows mean relative token-level accuracy drop <= 0.5% for FP8 and <= 1.5% for INT8 compared to the FP16 baseline.
P99 end-to-end latency for negotiated requests stays within configured SLAs for Dedicated customers in our staging env.
Validation pipeline produces daily reports of per-model, per-profile accuracy drift and stores artifacts (activation histograms, scale factors) for offline debugging.
Automated rollback/fallback triggers if validation detects sustained degradation for 6+ hours or a single spike > 3% absolute accuracy drop on critical prompts.
Unit and integration tests cover negotiation logic, telemetry tagging, and fallback paths.
Documentation describing configuration knobs (quality_budget, latency_budget, safety_threshold) merged in the runtime docs repo.
No critical security findings in a quick security review focusing on model artifact handling and telemetry privacy.
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight decision API: inputs = {model_id, request_slo_ms, quality_budget_pct, input_length_estimate, profile_hint}; output = {precision_plan, kernel_set, fallback_policy}.

Leverage existing quant profiles produced by the calibration pipeline (scale tensors, per-layer histograms). Negotiator must fall back to FP16 if profile artifacts are missing or calibration confidence is low.

Integrate a tiny on-request accuracy predictor (ML model or heuristic) that uses activation distribution similarity to calibration histograms to estimate accuracy risk; must be executable in <0.25ms in hot path.
Support per-layer overrides for sensitive modules (attention/query/key/value and final logits). Allow model owners to pin layers to FP16 via metadata.
Instrument telemetry: decision_reason tag, chosen_profile_id, predicted_risk_score, actual_perf/quality metrics for later reconciliation.
Validation pipeline: batch nightly job that replays a canonical prompt set across the candidate profiles and computes per-token and per-sequence regressions; store diffs and regression heatmaps.
Expose admin endpoint to force enable/disable profiles for a model and to trigger immediate re-evaluation of a profile.
Ensure compatibility with existing kernel loader and batching logic; kernel_set must be expressed as a stable identifier that the kernel router understands.
Plan staged rollout: canary to 5% of traffic (non-critical), expand to 50% after 48 hours if no alerts, full rollout gated on validation metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for the negotiation decision matrix with synthetic inputs (latency vs quality trade-offs).
Microbenchmarks for predictor latency and false-positive/false-negative rates on a held-out calibration set.
Integration test that deploys negotiator + kernel router in staging and runs simulated traffic with mixed prompt lengths to measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and failure modes.
Validation pipeline acceptance test that injects a known regression (scaled logits) and verifies automated rollback triggers are fired.
Backfill test harness to run overnight validation on previously seen production traces (anonymized) to estimate real-world accuracy impact.
Chaos test: temporarily remove calibration artifacts and verify negotiator falls back to safe FP16 paths without panics.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Predictor misestimates accuracy leading to silent regressions. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, daily validation with alerting, quick rollback path.
Risk: Added latency in hot path. Mitigation: keep decision logic <0.5ms; move heavier checks to async validation; cache decisions for repeated prompt patterns.
Risk: Inconsistent artifacts across model versions. Mitigation: require profile versioning and integrity checks; negotiator rejects unversioned profiles.
Risk: Telemetry overhead and privacy concerns. Mitigation: strip user-identifying fields; sample telemetry at 1% for verbose traces.
Risk: Interactions with batching causing suboptimal kernel mixes. Mitigation: coordinate with batching service to announce batch composition and include negotiator hints.
notes: Related calibration work: ensure quantizer outputs include confidence metadata (histogram entropy, outlier counts).
We should coordinate with Console team to show per-model profile health in the dashboard (labels: experimental, pinned, deprecated).
Prototype predictor could be a logistic regression on KL-divergence between runtime activations and calibration histograms; iterate to a small NN if needed.
